Preface: I came here after watching this video.

Hi!

I don't know much about fitness (as you'll probably realize) and I've always thought that muscle-mass increase is something that just happens if you're working out, especially with few reps / high load. Obviously not forgoing food or rest.

But what I'm wondering is, how do you know how much food you should eat? If you're having a too low nutritional intake compared to the amount of workout you're doing, will you know this simply by being hungry? So is the key to just make sure you're not hungry?
How do you know how much you need to eat?

You definitely won't be hungry at first, if at all. It's kind of the opposite of losing weight, where you would feel hungry all the time at first.

Generally, if you're not getting proper nutrition, you'll have food cravings. An example is when someone is low in magnesium, they'll sometimes crave chocolate, but not necessarily experience real hunger. Salt cravings can happen when you're low on many basic minerals or are dehydrated. It's important to understand cravings vs. hunger.

The best way to see how many calories you need to maintain your weight is to calculate your BMR (http://www.calculator.net/bmr-calculator.html). I have a crappy Chromebook and can't hyperlink, but there is one source for you. BMR is the minimum calories one needs per day, like if he/she were comatose. There are a couple of different formulas to calculate this, and you can add your activity level (sedentary, llight/moderate/heavy activity) to see how many you need to maintain with your activity level.

There are 3500 calories in a pound, so based on your activity level and BMR, you would add/deduct 3500 calories per week to gain or lose. Best way to do this if you're starting out is to track all of your calories. There are many free apps that can help you with this. Over time, you'll have a better understanding of how many calories are in various foods, as well as portion size, and can estimate calories better.

So, no, you won't feel hungry enough if you're exercising and trying to gain; some people feel stuffed when in the bulking phase, and it's difficult to get to the daily caloric intake. You'll still see progress, but you won't be as big if you're not watching your diet - same as weightloss.

I didn't watch the whole video, but in the beginning he mentions drinking milk and using smoothies to get the extra calories to gain. This is an easy way to get a couple hundred calories in because you can sip on it throughout the day, rather than trying to add an extra meal in - stomach can only handle so much food without proper training (like those pro hotdog eaters). A glass of whole milk (8 oz.) is about a hundred calories - swap that for water like he says, and you can easily get 300-500 extra calories in per day while getting some extra protein.

Finally, how do you know how much food you should eat? If you're just trying to maintain your weight, a good test is to eat slowly, and when you sigh during a meal, that is your stomach telling you you're full. It can take up to 20 minutes for the message of satiety to reach your brain from the stomach, the sigh is the first sign - you'll sigh a few minutes before actually "feeling full."
